absent: Full page, folio, zone, node and area structure layouts beyond the fields named here.
Real MMU fault handling, fixup and unmap flows; only no-MMU stubs are shown.
Lock ordering, sleeping rules and concurrency contracts for zap, lookup and reference paths.
Configuration conditions selecting each alt variant and hashed versus direct page addresses.
Exact numeric shifts, masks and flag bit positions for zone, node, section and sanitizer fields.
Pin-count storage, folio free path and batch release internals.
NUMA balancing policy for last-identity and access-time use.
Error-pointer encoding and maple-tree lookup guarantees.

findings.text: Transparent huge page helpers expose order and byte size for a compound page. The order helper first applies a page-flags debug check that the input is not a tail page, then reports the compound order. The size helper converts that order into bytes by scaling the base page size. Two build variants of the debug check exist, one delegating to a page check and one reducing to compile-time validation.

A page-table entry conditioning helper adds writability only when the owning virtual area allows writing. It inspects area write permission and, when present, passes the entry through a lower-level maker that ignores the area pointer and returns a writable entry. Otherwise the entry is returned unchanged.

Reference acquisition guards against zero or near-overflow counts before incrementing. One predicate reports the unsafe region using unsigned wrap arithmetic with a fixed margin. Folio acquisition asserts the predicate is false then increments. Page acquisition resolves the owning folio, refuses slab and large kmalloc folios with a one-time warning, then acquires the folio. Conditional page acquisition normalizes to the compound head, refuses non-positive counts, then increments and reports success.

Reference release decrements by one or many and frees on last drop. One helper subtracts a caller count and invokes the folio free path only when the count reaches zero. A batch helper forwards a folio batch to a refs variant with no auxiliary array. Page release resolves the folio, ignores slab and large kmalloc folios, otherwise releases one folio reference.

A transparent union provides three interchangeable views of a release list: an array of page pointers, an array of folio pointers, or an array of encoded page pointers. Callers may pass any one member where the union is expected.
The get-user-pages pin counting bias has numeric value one thousand twenty four, separating pin counts from ordinary reference counts.

Copy-on-write mapping status means may-write permission without shared permission. The predicate is evaluated on compact flag storage and reused for live areas and for area descriptors under construction.

Without an MMU, shared treatment applies to mappings marked may-share or may-overlay. One form tests raw flag bits and another tests the compact bitset for either of the two corresponding bits. Selected read-only private file overlays therefore count as shared for no-MMU purposes.

Several compile-time layout constants are defined: a marker that section numbers live in page flags, a marker for hashed page virtual addresses, a minimum access-time bit width of twelve, a derived bucket count that is either a shifted difference or zero depending on configuration, and a mask formed by shifting a last-identity mask by the bucket count.

Node, zone and section identity is extracted from packed flag words by shifting and masking with configuration-specific shifts and masks. Variants exist where node identity is always zero or section identity is always zero. Page and folio helpers resolve numeric node and zone identifiers and then index per-node zone arrays and node data to return zone and node descriptors.

Companion setters update the packed zone, node and section fields by clearing the field then inserting the masked value. A combined link helper sets zone and node together and, when sections live in flags, also records the section derived from the frame number.

CPU and process identity is packed into a small integer with separate subfields for each part. Helpers construct the value from a pair, extract each subfield, translate the CPU part to a node, test whether either subfield holds its all-ones unset pattern, and compare the stored process part against a task after masking. Disabled configurations return constant negative one, constant true for unset, or constant false for match, and report that access-time tracking is unused.

Per-folio last-access identity and coarse access time have multiple storage variants. In one variant a dedicated field is atomically exchanged under a mask and read directly, with reset writing the masked all-ones pattern; access time is exchanged by shifting through the bucket count. In a flag-packed variant the value lives in flag bits and reset sets those bits. In minimal variants exchange and read return the folio node or zero, and reset and per-area pid-bit recording become no-ops, while the enabled pid-bit path hashes the current process identifier into a bitmap in NUMA balancing state.

Per-page sanitizer tags are stored in flag bits in an inverted form with a kernel default. When the sanitizer is enabled the getter extracts and uninverts the field; otherwise it returns a fixed all-ones or kernel value. The setter uses a compare-and-exchange retry loop to replace only the tag field, and reset restores the kernel tag. Disabled builds provide empty setters.

Table entry constructors build entries from a page or folio frame number plus protection bits. Page frame number comes from the folio head page. Small entries use the frame entry constructor directly, while huge middle and upper level entries wrap the frame constructor with a huge marker.

Whether a folio may be pinned for direct memory access depends on a dedicated pin count when the folio is capable of carrying one, otherwise on whether the unsigned reference count reaches the pin bias. Capability depends on size and word width. A copy-for-DMA decision additionally requires that the address space has pinned memory and asserts that a write-protect sequence indicates protection is active.

Zero page detection compares a page frame number against a global zero frame, either by exact equality or by range membership within a zero mask depending on build. Folio detection delegates to the head page test.

Long-term pinnability excludes coherent device memory, file DAX memory, and, when migration types exist, contiguous and isolated blocks; the zero folio is explicitly allowed. Otherwise pinnability is the negation of zone-movable status. An alternate configuration allows every folio.

Folio geometry helpers report page count as one for small folios and the large count otherwise, compute a pointer to the immediately following folio, shift the base page shift by the folio order, and provide an architecture hook for making a folio accessible that succeeds unconditionally here.

Possibly-shared mapping status and expected reference count derive from mapping counts and folio state. Small and hugetlb folios use a simple greater-than-one test; partially mappable folios with at most one mapping report exclusive, otherwise consult a shared bit in MM identity tracking, with a fallback that assumes true when identity tracking is disabled. Expected count sums swap-cache, page-cache, private and per-mapping contributions with order scaling and warns on typed non-hugetlb pages.

Page address handling has direct and hashed variants. One build stores the virtual address in the page structure; another makes the setter a no-op. Initialization is a no-op in both shown variants. Low memory address translation delegates to the page-to-virtual conversion.

Reserve allocation status is recorded in the second bit of the least-recently-used list next pointer for both pages and folios. Test helpers report that bit, set writes a pointer value with only that bit set, and clear writes null. Callers that do not need the information may overwrite it.
Unmap control block carries an optional locked folio to unmap, flags to skip copy-on-write private pages, to reclaim page tables, and to indicate non-blocking reaping, plus extra zap flag bits.

Zap and copy control bits occupy low bit positions. Zap drop-marker and unmap occupy the first two bits. Memory-copy control defines try-change-writable, NUMA protection, userfault write-protect and resolve bits in the low four positions, with an all-write-protect combination covering both write-protect bits.

Frame-map lookup arguments separate inputs, internals and outputs. Inputs are an area pointer and a virtual address. Internals are a lock pointer and a table entry pointer that callers must not touch. Outputs report frame number, address mask, protection, writability and whether the mapping is a special real-frame map.

No-MMU fault and unmap entry points are stubs that always fail or do nothing, while lookup and range helpers delegate. The fault handler raises a bug and reports a bus error, the user-fault fixup raises a bug and reports a fault error, mapping unmaps are empty, shared-range unmap forwards with copy handling disabled, area lookup loads from the address-space maple tree, single-page remote acquisition validates flags and returns the page with its area, range zap covers the whole area, and lock capability reports false.

Synchronization for the examined helpers relies on atomic access rather than held locks in the visible code. Last-access identity exchange uses an atomic exchange, sanitizer tag update uses a read followed by a compare-and-exchange retry loop, pin state uses an atomic read, and frame-map lookup carries its lock pointer as opaque internal state owned by the callee.

Folio and page reference counts move from checked acquisition through shared use to conditional release. Acquisition is allowed only outside the zero-or-near-overflow region; release subtracts a count and triggers the free path exactly when the result reaches zero. Slab and large kmalloc pages bypass both acquisition and release, and conditional acquisition fails without increment when the head count is non-positive.

Several misuse paths are guarded or fatal. Near-overflow or zero acquisition triggers a folio debug check, slab or large kmalloc acquisition warns once and leaks no reference, conditional acquisition warns on non-positive counts, expected-count computation warns on typed non-hugetlb state, remote single-page acquisition rejects nowait mode and missing areas, DMA pin testing must use unsigned comparison to remain correct past signed overflow, reserve status is lost if list links are overwritten, and fault handling without an MMU ends in a bug.
